_purpose: Pre-registered mutant matrix for the n=21 tail-8 SAT calibration target (Sol reply 84 sec 6.5, sol/sol_reply_84_math11.md). Each mutant is a deliberate, documented weakening/error injected into search/sat/encode_tail8_n21.py's design, registered here BEFORE any solver run so that an observed verdict can be compared against a pre-committed prediction -- catching the case where a broken encoder silently produces a plausible-looking but wrong CNF. Baselines: tail8_n21_class.cnf expected SAT, tail8_n21_transitive.cnf expected UNSAT (search/sat/manifest_tail8_n21.json).
_note_on_confidence: Predictions below are either PROVEN (a short formal argument is given inline and can be checked on paper) or REASONED (a plausibility argument from group-theoretic facts already established in sol/sol_reply_84_math11.md sec F84-3.1, e.g. all 5 known C(u)-orbit representatives have orbit partition [6,15]) or UNKNOWN (explicitly flagged -- do not treat an UNKNOWN prediction's eventual solver output as self-validating; it needs a small independent oracle check, e.g. a bounded GAP census, before being trusted as a caught bug vs. a coincidence).
_addendum_ruling214_step4: Entries M8-M12 below were added per sol/sol_reply_85_math12.md P85-6 (Sol's 'next SAT hardening' priority list, delivered to the mathematician/commander via F85-8.5's assessment that M1/M3/M4 UNKNOWN rows are honest but not yet closed, and M6 is 'weak' because its instance is disconnected -- a depth-1-off test is not decisive there). M8/M9 instantiate P85-6 points 1-2 (reverse-clause-drop mutants), M10 instantiates point 3 (synthetic diameter-20 boundary fixture, explicitly built to REPLACE M6 as the decisive depth-boundary check; M6 itself is kept below unmodified as a historical row, not deleted). M11 instantiates point 4 (n=5,7 exhaustive calibration, run locally -- not solver output, ground truth from itertools/BFS plus an encoding-fidelity spot check). M12 documents point 5 (independent LRAT checker, implemented from scratch and run against the real n=21 transitive proof, not just self-tests). kissat was NOT invoked for M8/M9/M10 here (RAM 8GB constraint; CI dispatch is the commander's job) -- only CNF generation and paper-proof expected verdicts are registered; the CI run and comparison against these predictions is future work.

mutants.description: Flip the product order used to derive b from a: instead of b=a*u^-1 (i.e. b(i)=u^-1(a(i))), derive b'=u^-1*a (i.e. b'(i)=a(u^-1(i))). Concretely: B'[i][k] <-> (D[j] if j==k else X[j,k]) where j=u^-1(i), i.e. index by a(u^-1(i)) instead of u^-1(a(i)).

prediction.class_cnf_argument: b' = u^-1*a = u^-1*(b*u) = u^-1*b*u (using a=b*u from the baseline b=a*u^-1), i.e. b' is a CONJUGATE of the baseline b by u^-1. Conjugation preserves cycle type, so b' is fixed-point-free of type 3^7 whenever b is. Reusing the SAME a from any baseline witness (e.g. search/sat/fixtures/witness_n21_nontransitive.json) gives a valid model for the flipped scheme. So class-only SAT is preserved, just with a different decoded b.
prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: Transitivity of <a, u^-1*b*u> is not determined by transitivity of <a,b> alone -- only b is conjugated, not a, so the two generated groups are not simply conjugate to each other. Needs a small independent GAP/oracle check over a handful of known (a,b) pairs before this row is trusted either way.
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: If class_cnf run: decoded a should still be type 2^10 1 (unchanged constraint), decoded b should be type 3^7 but in general NOT equal to the baseline fixture's b (different indexing).

mutants.description: Drop u^-1 entirely: set b:=a directly, i.e. B[i][k] <-> (D[i] if k==i else X[i,k]) -- literally alias B to A's own matrix instead of routing through u.

prediction.class_cnf_argument: With this alias, the fixed-point-free clauses (not B[i][i] for all i) become (not D[i] for all i), which directly contradicts the diagonal exactly-one-of-21 constraint on D[1..21] (a_diagonal_exactly_one_fixed_point requires exactly one D[i] true; fixed-point-free forces all of them false). This is a unit-propagation-level contradiction, i.e. UNSAT should be found essentially immediately by any solver (a useful trivial-UNSAT sanity mutant, distinct from the 'real' UNSAT of the transitivity target).
prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: transitive.cnf's clause set is a superset of class.cnf's clauses, so UNSAT of the class-only subset implies UNSAT of the whole.
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: N/A -- expected UNSAT before any model exists. If a solver reports SAT here, that is itself a definite bug signal (the class-only contradiction above is elementary).

mutants.description: Drop the GLOBAL diagonal exactly-one-of-21 constraint (group a_diagonal_exactly_one_fixed_point in the manifest) while keeping the per-row exactly-one. Row exactly-one alone only guarantees a is SOME involution (any odd number 1,3,...,21 of fixed points), not specifically type 2^10 1.

prediction.class_cnf_argument: Removing a clause group from an already-SAT instance cannot make it UNSAT (strictly weaker constraint set; every previous model remains a model).
prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: Widening a's admissible cycle types to any odd-fixed-point involution changes the search space for the transitivity goal in a way not covered by the existing 2^10 1-only census (search/probe/wac_v1/tail8_exact.g only enumerated the 2^10 1 case). Could plausibly become SAT via an involution of a different type generating a transitive group -- not ruled out on paper here.
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: If SAT: the checker's independent a_is_involution_type_2^10_1 check (search/sat/check_model_n21.mjs) is EXPECTED to report ok:false for the decoded model, since the search space now includes non-2^10-1 involutions and nothing biases the solver toward the 'intended' type. A model that happens to still be type 2^10 1 is not a bug, just an unconstrained coincidence.

mutants.description: Drop either the b_cubed_equals_identity clause group or the b_fixed_point_free clause group (two sub-variants: M4a drops b^3=1, M4b drops fixed-point-free).

prediction.class_cnf_argument: Strict weakening of an already-SAT instance (same argument as M3).
prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: Widening b's admissible cycle types (e.g. allowing 1-cycles if fpf is dropped, or allowing non-order-3 permutations if b^3=1 is dropped) could plausibly let <a,b> become transitive for some pair not in the 3^7-restricted census. Not ruled out on paper.
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: If SAT: checker's b_is_fixed_point_free / b_cubed_equals_identity / b_is_type_3^7 checks are expected to be able to report ok:false for the decoded b (no encoding-side pressure toward 3^7 anymore); a coincidental 3^7 decode is not a bug.

mutants.description: Drop the entire transitivity apparatus (E/STEP/R groups and the goal clauses) from tail8_n21_transitive.cnf, i.e. this mutant of CNF#2 reduces exactly to CNF#1.

prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: By construction this mutant's clause set is byte-identical to tail8_n21_class.cnf's clause set (variables above CLASS_VAR_COUNT simply do not appear), whose SAT status is already established (search/sat/fixtures/witness_n21_nontransitive.json is an explicit satisfying assignment, independently checked in scratchpad/verify_class_cnf.mjs: 0/14806 clauses violated).
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: Decoded model satisfies all class checks; transitivity is UNCONSTRAINED so the model may or may not happen to be transitive (the known census says none of the 4160 solutions are, so in practice expect non-transitive, but this mutant's CNF does not encode that fact either way).

mutants.status: HISTORICAL -- kept unmodified, not deleted. Sol F85-8.5 (sol_reply_85_math12.md) assessed this row as 'weak' since the n=21 instance's true bottleneck is disconnection (orbit partition [6,15]), not an insufficient depth bound, so a depth-1-off test on THIS instance is not decisive. Superseded as the depth-boundary check by M10_synthetic_diam20_path (search/sat/encode_diam20_path21.py, P85-6 point 3), a purpose-built 21-vertex path fixture whose true diameter from vertex 1 is exactly 20.
mutants.description: Reduce the BFS depth bound from 0..20 (21 layers, matching the 21-point diameter bound) to 0..19 (20 layers), i.e. drop the t=20 layer and require R[19][v] for all v as the goal instead of R[20][v].

prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: GAP's independent report (sol/sol_reply_84_math11.md F84-3.1, and the machine-extracted fixture here) is that the actual orbit partition for every known solution is [6,15] -- i.e. the relevant Cayley graphs are NOT connected at all (two separate orbits), so no amount of extra BFS depth would ever connect them; the true obstruction is disconnection, not an insufficient depth bound. Shrinking the depth by 1 therefore should not flip this specific instance's verdict away from UNSAT. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this reasoning is instance-specific, not a general validation of the depth-1-off mutant methodology -- for THIS n=21 instance, a depth-sensitivity test is not very informative because true diameter (within each of the two orbits) is far below 20 already. A more decisive depth-boundary test would need a synthetically constructed instance whose true diameter is exactly 20 or 19 (deferred; not built here).
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: N/A (still UNSAT expected); if this mutant instead comes out SAT, that is a genuine and interesting signal worth investigating (would mean either the depth bound in the baseline was over-generous, or something is wrong elsewhere).

prediction.transitive_cnf_argument: Dropping R[t][v] => R[t-1][v] v (OR_w STEP[t][w][v]) removes the only constraint that could ever force an R variable to FALSE; every R[t][v] can be set true with zero justification (the kept sufficient direction is an implication INTO R, satisfied vacuously by R=true). Setting all R[t>=1][v]=true in particular satisfies the transitivity goal clauses (R[20][v] for all v) regardless of the actual graph structure -- a solver should find this trivially SAT, and this is exactly the 'BFS free-true' bug the mutant is designed to catch: if a run on THIS mutant instead comes out UNSAT, that is a definite bug signal in the R-variable wiring (not a coincidence needing an oracle check).
prediction.decoded_counterexample_property: If SAT: the decoded R assignment is expected to NOT correspond to any honest BFS reachability set (check_model_n21.mjs's independent BFS recomputation, run against this mutant's model, is expected to disagree with the model's own R/STEP variables for at least the un-actually-reached vertices -- that disagreement is the signature of the caught bug, not evidence against the mutant).

actual_run.check_model_n21_mjs: run --mode transitive against the SAT model: overall ok=false -- decoded a,b satisfy all involution/order/type checks and the independently recomputed b=u^-1(a(.)) agrees with the model's B variables, BUT the generated group <a,b> is NOT transitive on 1..21 (orbits [6,15]). This is exactly the predicted bug signature (decoded_counterexample_property): the SAT model's own R/reachability variables claim full reachability while the underlying permutation group demonstrably is not transitive, confirming the R-wiring bug the mutant targets.
actual_run.artifact_note: SAT model (kissat 'v ...' lines) preserved as model_vlines.txt; check_model_n21.mjs raw output preserved as check_model_output.txt.

Setting all E[i][j]=true turns the Cayley graph into the complete graph K_21 (diameter 1), so the still-intact R/STEP Tseitin machinery correctly derives R[t][v]=true for all v already at t=1<=20, satisfying the transitivity goal regardless of the actual {a,b,b^-1} adjacency. If a run on this mutant instead comes out UNSAT, that is a definite bug signal in the E-variable wiring.

mutants.description: P85-6 point 4. n=5,7 exhaustive calibration of the general class-constraint + BFS-transitivity encoding MACHINERY (not a reproduction of the n=21 target's exact axioms -- b_fixed_point_free is dropped since 3 does not divide 5 or 7, see search/sat/calibrate_small_n.py module docstring for the full relaxation rationale). Ground truth via pure Python itertools/BFS (no GAP, no SAT solver), fixed u = the n-cycle (1 2 ... n) for each n. A parameterized CNF encoder (self-contained duplicate of the X/D/B/E/STEP/R scheme, not importing encode_tail8_n21.py) is also built and, for each ground-truth witness found, an encoding-fidelity spot check evaluates EVERY generated clause against the witness-derived assignment (no solver -- direct clause evaluation).
